section2.title: The app that turns surplus food into savings
section2.description: A marketplace for food that has not sold yet. Shops list what is left before they close, and people nearby collect it the same day at a fraction of the price.

benefits.saveMoney: GOOD FOOD AT HALF PRICE OR LESS
benefits.earnPoints: FOOD THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN THROWN AWAY

dream.standfirst: Every city on earth throws food away at closing time. Not because anyone wants to - because there was no way to sell it in the hour that was left. We built that way. We started with one city, and the people in each city decide which one comes next.

problem.title: Food does not go to waste. It gets left behind.
problem.body1: A bakery closing at seven has bread it cannot sell at eight. A grocer has fruit that is perfect today and unsellable tomorrow. None of it is spoiled and none of it is wanted, because the only buyer left is the bin.
problem.body2: That is not a moral failure. It is a timing problem - and timing problems are solvable. What was missing was a way to reach the people nearby in the last hour, at a price that makes the trip worth it for both sides.
problem.pullquote: Nobody wakes up wanting to throw away what they made that morning.

wins.title: Every side of this has to win, or none of it lasts.

merchant.what: Surplus becomes revenue instead of a disposal cost. You set the price, you set the quantity, and you keep 81% of every bag.

customer.what: Real food from a real shop nearby, at a fraction of the price, collected the same day. Not charity, not leftovers - the same food, later in the day.

planet.what: Food thrown away has already cost the water, land and fuel that produced it. Rescuing a bag saves all of it, not just the meal.

neighbour.what: Part of the platform margin funds a rotating donation goal, so the same surplus that pays a merchant also puts something back on a local family shelf.

proof.note: Live totals from the platform. When there is nothing to report yet, this shows a dash rather than a zero.

close.title: Tunisia first. Then everywhere that closes with food still on the shelf.
close.body: Algeria, Morocco, the Gulf - the problem is identical in all of them, and so is the fix. But it only travels if it works here first, and that starts with one more business in one more city.

faq1.question: How does Too Fresh To Waste work?
faq1.answer: Too Fresh To Waste connects you with local restaurants, bakeries, hotels, and grocery stores that have surplus food. Browse offers near you, reserve your meal, pay securely, and pick it up at the designated time or choose home delivery. It's that simple!

faq2.question: What is the business solution?
faq2.answer:
PROFIT FROM YOUR SURPLUS FOOD

Our marketplace connects your business with users across Tunisia - all eager to buy surplus food.

faq3.question: How does the Big Prize work?
faq3.answer: The Big Prize is awarded every six months, and it unlocks once we have rescued 30,000 bags together. Every bag anyone saves counts towards it, so it is won as a community rather than alone. You improve your own chances by buying surprise bags, referring friends or businesses, leaving honest reviews, and logging in daily.

faq4.question: What is in the Big Prize?
faq4.answer:
Three days in a hotel
An electric scooter
A full year of gym membership
A phone
A voucher to spend on clothes
faq4.intro: Every six months, once we have rescued 30,000 bags together, the list opens and the winner chooses which prize they want.

pledge.body: True change doesn't ask you to pay extra. We automatically dedicate 5% of our net profits from every surplus bag sold on our marketplace. Whether you are buying a meal or selling one, you are actively funding human dignity - without spending a single extra dinar.

items.title: Zero Hungry Nights
items.body: We transform food waste revenue into actual groceries and meals for families facing extreme poverty. No family should ever have to put their young children to bed hungry.

items.title: Dignity for the Elderly
items.body: Many grandparents cannot afford essential treatments. We directly fund pharmacies to cover the cost of chronic medications for elderly patients without a safety net.

items.title: Empowering the Next Generation
items.body: A bright mind should never be kept out of the classroom due to a lack of funds. We provide school supplies and cover education fees so children can build a better future.

items.title: Warmth & Care
items.body: Every season brings new hardships. We provide essential clothing to ensure that vulnerable individuals and families stay warm, protected, and treated with respect.

partner.headline: Fueled by Tunisian Businesses.
partner.body: This impact is entirely made possible by the restaurants, bakeries, hotels, patisseries, grocery stores, supermarkets, and enterprise companies using our app. Every time your company uses Too Fresh To Waste, you receive a monthly impact report showing exactly how many lives your daily operations helped transform.

hero.subtitle: The Parcless Bag transforms your unsold stock and production surplus into real revenue - while reducing your environmental footprint and feeding Tunisian families.

concept.label: The concept
concept.body1: The Parcless Bag is an anti-waste solution designed for Tunisian manufacturers. You package your unsold items, surplus or products near their expiry date in a discounted mystery bag. Consumers buy it through our app - and everyone wins.
concept.body2: Inspired by the global success of Too Good To Go, the Parcless Bag is adapted to Tunisian market realities: local logistics, consumption habits and strong social impact.
concept.statDesc: of partner manufacturers reduce their food waste rate by 70 to 80% in under 3 months.

howItWorks.label: How it works
howItWorks.subtitle: Three steps to turn your surplus into revenue and your commitment into real impact.

steps.title: You prepare the bag
steps.body: Each evening - or at your chosen frequency - your teams package the day's surplus in a standardised Parcless Bag. Real value: 2 to 3× the selling price on the app.

problem.p1: Bakeries, restaurants, hotels, and supermarkets across Tunisia discard between 10 and 20% of their daily production every single evening. Not because the food is bad - because the shelf ran out of time. (WRAP)
problem.p2: The economic cost of global food waste is estimated at <fao>$1 trillion per year</fao> (FAO, 2014) - a figure that excludes the environmental cost. When food decomposes in landfill, it releases methane, a gas <epa>80 times more potent than CO₂</epa> over a 20-year period (US EPA).
problem.p3: Tunisia alone generates <unep>172 kg of food waste per person per year</unep> - the highest rate in the Maghreb.

solution.lede: The Too Fresh To Waste platform lets food businesses list surplus inventory as discounted "Surprise Bags" - claimed by customers before closing time, every day.
